name: Client Lines
tagline: The right message for every client moment
about: Client Lines writes the messages freelancers dread: the weekly update, the 'we're going to be late' note, the reply to vague or conflicting feedback, the nudge when a client goes silent, and the welcome pack that sets expectations from day one.
persona: You are a calm, plain-spoken account manager for solo professionals: honest about problems, generous with context, never grovelling, always ending with a clear next step.

onboarding.title: Say it right the first time
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your work and your voice so every message sounds like you.

tools.title: Welcome pack
tools.subtitle: How I work, for new clients
tools.prompt: Write a welcome pack for {client} communicating via {channel} with {rounds} revision rounds included. Sections: a kv (working hours from the profile, response time, single point of contact, feedback format, revision rounds, how to flag urgent), a table (Phase | What I need from you | What you'll get | When) with 4–6 phases for the project, a quote with the covering message in the profile voice, and a callout on the three expectations that prevent most mid-project friction.

tools.title: Weekly client update
tools.subtitle: Progress, next, needs

inputs.label: This week
inputs.placeholder: finished checkout, waiting on their product photos, found a bug in the old CMS

tools.prompt: Write this week's update from: {progress}. Next week: {next}. Produce a quote with the message (done, in progress, next, what I need from you, any risk) under 180 words in the profile voice, a checklist of items the client owes you with suggested due dates, and a callout on any risk in the notes that deserves a direct sentence rather than a soft hint.

tools.title: We're going to be late
tools.subtitle: Deliver the delay with a plan

inputs.label: What happened and how late
inputs.placeholder: their API access came 8 days late; delivery slips 1 week

tools.prompt: Delay: {why}. Cause: {fault}. Give a text section on how to frame it for that cause (no over-apologising if it's the client's), a quote with the delay notice including the new date, what you're doing to reduce the slip and one option for the client, bullets of 3 concessions you can offer that cost you little, and a callout on the contract or change-order note to add if the cause is the client's.

tools.title: Decode their feedback
tools.subtitle: Vague or conflicting notes → questions

inputs.label: Paste the feedback
inputs.placeholder: 'make it pop', 'less corporate', CEO wants blue, marketing wants green

tools.prompt: Feedback received: {feedback}. Produce a table (Comment | What they might mean | Concrete options | Question to ask), a text section spotting conflicts between stakeholders and who should arbitrate, a quote with a reply that lists your interpretation, at most 4 crisp questions and a proposed decision deadline, and a callout on how to count this against the revision rounds.

tools.title: Client went quiet
tools.subtitle: Nudges that get a reply
tools.prompt: Waiting {days} days on: {waiting}, stage: {stage}. Produce a table (Nudge | Day to send | Channel | Tone) for a 3-message sequence, a quote for each of the 3 messages in the profile voice with the third setting a gentle deadline and stating what happens next, and a callout on how to protect the schedule and payment while paused.
